checks: For bounded finite source volume, the feasible densities are weak-* compact in L∞ and the finitely many mass and moment functionals are weak-* continuous. Thus the prescribed raw moment set is nonempty, convex and compact.

For every feasible density, (L_i)_+≥fL_i gives the raw support bound with additive term t_z(a_i·z−b_i). At a supported saddle pair, zero positively weighted margins and continuous-normal balance cancel these affine terms.
The ellipsoid support is u_i·c_z+|A_zᵀu_i|. Its center cancels at each pair, with no separate optimization of the prescribed cap tilts.

The frozen stress supplies finite supported probability pairs, nonnegative coverage weights and exactly the W_i offset identity at the same selected representative. Feasible masses remain the bridge’s own assumption; a trivial mass zero always exists and a sampled positive fiber itself gives a feasible positive same-base mass.
Compared exact original and revised inputs. The only change is the two added statements specifying nonnegative η_z and summation over bases of positive weight.
Matched each cited source locator to the exact preserved source candidate and verified its pinned bytes and frozen source SHA-256.

issues.defect: The hypotheses give measures only at η_z>0, but the stated sums are unqualified and η_z is not constrained to be nonnegative. The proof uses nonnegative weighted summation. With unrestricted signed sums, take one fiber [0,1], margins x and −x, η=−1, λ=(1/2,1/2) at x=0 and t=1. The two support terms cancel, but the weighted hinge sum is −1/4.
issues.locator: Statement, definition of η_z, ν_z and W_i
issues.repair: Require η_z≥0 and say that the sums involving ν_z or Q_z run over bases of positive weight.

overlap.comparison: The accepted John-contact theorem starts by choosing supporting directions and finite original-source tilts at one prescribed interior mass. This bridge instead tests a fixed source-cap family and pre-existing saddle weights at possibly different feasible masses, using their zero-margin balance to remove the affine costs.

initial_review.readability: The source normality theorem uses nonnegative multipliers. The standalone statement needs the same condition before the bridge is applied to arbitrary pairs.
